config.title: useId & Stable IDs

intro.title: useId & Stable IDs
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue component that generates and displays unique, stable IDs for form elements. You will learn the core concept of using a composable function, `useId`, to create identifiers that remain consistent across component renders, preventing mismatches in server-side rendering and hydration. The main technologies involved are Vue's Composition API and the `useId` utility. This practice is essential for accessibility and form handling in dynamic applications. By the end, you'll understand how to implement stable IDs to improve your app's reliability.
intro.usecase: In real-world Vue applications, stable IDs are essential for accessibility and form functionality. When building complex forms with multiple input fields, each label needs a unique ID that matches its corresponding input's `for` attribute for proper screen reader support. In dynamic dashboards with collapsible panels or accordions, stable IDs ensure ARIA attributes like `aria-controls` and `aria-labelledby` maintain correct relationships as components re-render. This pattern also prevents ID collisions in reusable components like modals, tabs, or data tables where multiple instances might appear on the same page.

objectives: Implement the useId composable to generate unique identifiers within a Vue component.
Apply stable IDs to form elements like labels and inputs to ensure proper accessibility.
Construct a component that dynamically renders multiple elements, each with a stable ID.
Configure a reusable composable that leverages useId for custom ID generation logic.
Update an existing component to replace hardcoded IDs with stable IDs from useId.
Integrate stable IDs with ARIA attributes to enhance component accessibility.
Manipulate ID generation by passing custom prefixes to the useId composable.

steps.title: Add name input field with stable ID
steps.instruction: Inside the form, add a text input field for the name with v-model binding to the reactive data and use the generated stable ID for the 'id' attribute.
steps.hint: Use the generated ID from useId for the input's id attribute and bind the input value to the reactive form data using v-model.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: input field with stable ID and v-model
<input type="text" :id="nameId" v-model="formData.name" placeholder="Enter your name">
steps.seedCode:
<script setup>
import { useId } from 'vue'
// Call useId to generate a stable ID for form fields
const nameId = useId()

// Create reactive form data here
const formData = {
  name: ''
}

// Define form submission handler here
const handleSubmit = () => {
  console.log('Form submitted:', formData)
}
</script>

<template>
  <form @submit.prevent="handleSubmit">
    <!-- Add name input field here -->
  </form>
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have a text input field for the name, bound to the reactive data and using the stable ID from useId.
successCriteria: The input field has :id="nameId", v-model="formData.name", and is placed inside the form.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input field, but make sure it has both :id="nameId" and v-model="formData.name" attributes.
